sodium.options.view_distance.tooltip: The render distance controls how far away terrain will be rendered. Shorter distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates.
sodium.options.simulation_distance.toolt: The simulation distance controls how far away terrain and entities will be loaded and ticked. Shorter distances can reduce the internal server's load and may improve frame rates.
sodium.options.brightness.tooltip: Controls the minimum brightness in the world. When increased, darker areas of the world will appear brighter. This does not affect the brightness of already well-lit areas.
sodium.options.gui_scale.tooltip: Sets the maximum scale factor to be used for the user interface. If "auto" is used, then the largest scale factor will always be used.
sodium.options.fullscreen_mode.name: Fullscreen Mode
sodium.options.fullscreen_mode.tooltip: Exclusive fullscreen can improve latency, but may prevent some input methods from working and slow down switching out of the game. Borderless fullscreen can cause significant performance degradation.
sodium.options.fullscreen_resolution.too: The monitor resolution and refresh rate to be used when in fullscreen mode. Changing this option may interfere with other applications and cause a delay when switching between applications.
sodium.options.v_sync.tooltip: If enabled, the game's frame rate will be synchronized to the monitor's refresh rate, making for a generally smoother experience at the expense of overall input latency. This setting might reduce performance if your system is too slow.
sodium.options.fps_limit.tooltip: Limits the maximum number of frames per second. This can help reduce battery usage and system load when multi-tasking. If VSync is enabled, this option will be ignored unless it is lower than your display's refresh rate.
sodium.options.attack_indicator.tooltip: Controls where the Attack Indicator is displayed on screen.
sodium.options.autosave_indicator.toolti: If enabled, an indicator will be shown when the game is saving the world to disk.
sodium.options.graphics_quality.tooltip: The default graphics quality controls some legacy options and is necessary for mod compatibility. If the options below are left to "Default", they will use this setting.
sodium.options.clouds_quality.tooltip: The quality level used for rendering clouds in the sky. Even though the options are labeled "Fast" and "Fancy", the effect on performance is negligible.
sodium.options.clouds_distance.tooltip: The distance clouds will render to. This has minimal impact on performance, and is meant for visual purposes.
sodium.options.weather_quality.tooltip: Controls the distance that weather effects, such as rain and snow, will be rendered.
sodium.options.leaves_quality.name: Leaves
sodium.options.leaves_quality.tooltip: Controls whether leaves will be rendered as transparent (fancy) or opaque (fast).
sodium.options.particle_quality.tooltip: Controls the maximum number of particles which can be present on screen at any one time.
sodium.options.smooth_lighting.tooltip: Enables the smooth lighting and shading of blocks in the world. This can very slightly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update a chunk, but it doesn't affect frame rates.
sodium.options.biome_blend.tooltip: The area (in blocks) where biome colors are smoothly blended across. Default is 5x5. Higher values will greatly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update chunks, for diminishing improvements in quality.
sodium.options.entity_distance.tooltip: The render distance multiplier used by entity rendering. Smaller values decrease, and larger values increase, the maximum distance at which entities will be rendered.
sodium.options.entity_shadows.tooltip: If enabled, basic shadows will be rendered beneath mobs and other entities.
sodium.options.vignette.name: Vignette
sodium.options.vignette.tooltip: If enabled, a vignette effect will be applied when the player is in darker areas, which makes the overall image darker and more dramatic.
sodium.options.mipmap_levels.tooltip: Controls the number of mipmaps which will be used for block model textures. Higher values provide better rendering of blocks in the distance, but could adversely affect performance with resource packs that use many animated textures.
sodium.options.use_block_face_culling.to: If enabled, only the faces of blocks which are facing the camera will be submitted for rendering. This can eliminate a large number of block faces very early in the rendering process, which greatly improves rendering performance. Some resource packs may have issues with this option, so try disabling it if you're seeing holes in blocks.
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.name: Use Fog Occlusion
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.tooltip: If enabled, chunks which are determined to be fully hidden by fog effects will not be rendered, helping to improve performance. The improvement can be more dramatic when fog effects are heavier (such as while underwater), but it may cause undesirable visual artifacts between the sky and fog in some scenarios.
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.name: Use Entity Culling
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.toolti: If enabled, entities which are within the camera viewport, but not inside of a visible chunk, will be skipped during rendering. This optimization uses the visibility data which already exists for chunk rendering and does not add overhead.
sodium.options.animate_only_visible_text: If enabled, only the animated textures which are determined to be visible in the current image will be updated. This can provide a significant performance improvement on some hardware, especially with heavier resource packs. If you experience issues with some textures not being animated, try disabling this option.
sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead_limit.to: For debugging only. Specifies the maximum number of frames which can be in-flight to the GPU. Changing this value is not recommended, as very low or high values may create frame rate instability.
sodium.options.use_persistent_mapping.to: This is now always on if supported.
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.name: Chunk Update Threads
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.tool: Specifies the number of threads to use for chunk building and sorting. Using more threads can speed up chunk loading and update speed, but may negatively impact frame times. The default value is usually good enough for all situations.
sodium.options.defer_chunk_updates.name: Chunk Updates
sodium.options.defer_chunk_updates.toolt: If set to "Deferred", rendering will never wait for nearby chunk updates to finish, even if they are important. This can greatly improve frame rates in some scenarios, but it may create significant visual lag where blocks take a while to appear or disappear. "Immediate" eliminates visual lag by blocking the frame until chunk updates are complete while "Soon" allows at most one frame of visual lag.
sodium.options.quad_splitting.name: Block Transparency Limits
sodium.options.quad_splitting.tooltip: Determines what approach is used to make translucent blocks (not entities or items) look correct even when they intersect or have unusual shapes, such as waterlogged stained glass panes. "Basic" disables this feature and such blocks may render incorrectly. "Safe" limits the amount of newly generated geometry to prevent instability in extreme cases, while "Unlimited" imposes no limit.
sodium.options.position_bits_x.name: Position Bits (X)
sodium.options.position_bits_y.name: Position Bits (Y)
sodium.options.position_bits_z.name: Position Bits (Z)
sodium.options.position_bits_x.tooltip: How many bits are used to store the horizontal (east-west) position of terrain vertices. All three axes share a single 32-bit value, and each axis spends one extra bit on an endpoint, so the three sliders must total no more than 29 bits. If they total more, the axes are reduced automatically. Fewer bits means blocks can sit slightly away from their true position; more bits reduces that error, halving it with every extra bit. 10 bits keeps it under 0.02 blocks, 11 bits under 0.01. Vertex memory use never changes, as every setting still packs into the same 16 bytes per vertex.
sodium.options.position_bits_y.tooltip: How many bits are used to store the vertical position of terrain vertices. All three axes share a single 32-bit value, and each axis spends one extra bit on an endpoint, so the three sliders must total no more than 29 bits. If they total more, the axes are reduced automatically. Fewer bits means blocks can sit slightly away from their true position; more bits reduces that error, halving it with every extra bit. 10 bits keeps it under 0.02 blocks, 11 bits under 0.01. Vertex memory use never changes, as every setting still packs into the same 16 bytes per vertex.
sodium.options.position_bits_z.tooltip: How many bits are used to store the horizontal (north-south) position of terrain vertices. All three axes share a single 32-bit value, and each axis spends one extra bit on an endpoint, so the three sliders must total no more than 29 bits. If they total more, the axes are reduced automatically. Fewer bits means blocks can sit slightly away from their true position; more bits reduces that error, halving it with every extra bit. 10 bits keeps it under 0.02 blocks, 11 bits under 0.01. Vertex memory use never changes, as every setting still packs into the same 16 bytes per vertex.
sodium.options.hidden_fluid_culling.name: Fluid Culling
sodium.options.hidden_fluid_culling.tool: Controls how aggressively hidden fluid surfaces are culled. "Optimized" applies more aggressive culling to fluids, which can improve performance in flooded caves and underwater areas, but interruptions in the fluid surface may rarely become visible at very shallow viewing angles. "Default" keeps the standard culling behavior.
sodium.options.improved_fluid_shaping.to: Controls how fluids are shaped around waterlogged blocks. "Alternative" can improve the consistency of fluid surfaces, at the expense of not slanting the fluid in the direction of the physical flow in some situations. This does not affect the physical behavior of fluids in any way.
sodium.options.closest_point_entity_sort: Controls how the translucent geometry of entities is sorted. "Enhanced" sorts by the closest point to the camera, which improves rendering accuracy for translucent quads with different sizes, at a small CPU cost. "Default" uses the standard sorting.
sodium.options.pixel_filtering_mode.name: Texel Interpolation
sodium.options.pixel_filtering_mode.tool: Controls the appearance of edges between pixels within block textures. "Nearest" mode results in sharp pixel boundaries, while "Linear" mode makes them a little blurry. "Nearest" can be slightly faster.
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.name: Use No Error Context
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.tool: When enabled, the OpenGL context will be created with error checking disabled. This slightly improves rendering performance, but it can make debugging sudden unexplained crashes much harder.
sodium.console.game_restart: The game must be restarted to apply one or more video settings!

sodium.console.core_shaders_warn: The following resource packs may be incompatible with Sodium:
sodium.console.core_shaders_info: Check the game log for detailed information.
sodium.console.config_not_loaded: The configuration file for Sodium has been corrupted, or is currently unreadable. Some options have been temporarily reset to their defaults. Please open the Video Settings screen to resolve this problem.
sodium.console.corrupt_config.console.co: The config file has been reset to known-good defaults.
sodium.console.corrupt_config.console.ti: Sodium failed to load the configuration file
sodium.console.corrupt_config.message.ti: Could not load the configuration file
sodium.console.corrupt_config.message.bo:
A problem occurred while trying to load the configuration file. This
can happen when the file has been corrupted on disk, or when trying
to manually edit the file by hand.

If you continue, the configuration file will be reset back to known-good
defaults, and you will lose any changes that have since been made to your
Video Settings.

More information about the error can be found in the log file.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.enabled.name: Celestial Shadows
sodium.options.sky_shadows.enabled.toolt:
Casts directional shadows from the sun and moon, so terrain shadows follow the light instead of staying fixed to the block grid.

Runs a second depth-only pass over nearby terrain, so this costs frames on top of normal rendering. Off by default.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.colors.name: Sunset Colours
sodium.options.sky_shadows.colors.toolti:
Tints the direct light as it approaches the horizon.

Turn this off to see the shadows on their own, without colour grading.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.filter_sample:
How many depth samples each shadowed fragment compares.

1 gives a hard edge for less cost; 4 smooths the edge with a filtered reconstruction.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.near_resoluti:
Width in texels of the cascade covering blocks close to you.

Higher values sharpen contact shadows near your feet at a cost in memory and render time.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.near_radius.t: How far in blocks the near cascade reaches before the far cascade takes over.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.far_resolutio:
Width in texels of the cascade covering distant terrain.

This usually needs fewer texels than the near cascade because the shadows are spread much wider.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.far_radius.to:
How far in blocks shadows are drawn before they fade out.

Always kept at least 16 blocks beyond the near radius so the two cascades do not overlap.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.base_bias.too:
How far a fragment is pushed towards the light before comparing depths.

Raise this if shadows detach from the surfaces casting them; lower it if surfaces shadow themselves.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.ambient.name: Shadowed Ambient
sodium.options.sky_shadows.ambient.toolt:
How much light a fully shadowed surface keeps.

Higher values make shadow interiors brighter and softer; lower values make them darker and more defined.
How strongly the sun lights surfaces during the day.
sodium.options.sky_shadows.moon_strength:
How strongly the moon lights surfaces at night.

Usually kept well below Sun Strength so night shadows stay dark.
sodium.options.bloom.name: Bloom
sodium.options.bloom.tooltip:
Adds a soft glow around bright areas such as the sun, torches and lava.

Runs as a screen-space effect after the world is rendered.
sodium.options.bloom_intensity.name: Bloom Intensity
sodium.options.bloom_intensity.tooltip:
How strongly the glow is added on top of the scene.

At 0% bloom is disabled without changing any other setting.
sodium.options.bloom_threshold.name: Bloom Threshold
sodium.options.bloom_threshold.tooltip:
How bright a pixel has to be before it starts to glow.

Raising this keeps only the brightest highlights; lowering it makes the whole image glow.
sodium.options.bloom_radius.name: Bloom Radius
sodium.options.bloom_radius.tooltip:
How far the glow spreads.

Higher values produce a wider, softer halo.
sodium.options.tonemap.name: Tonemapping
sodium.options.tonemap.tooltip:
Applies a tone curve to the final image to roll off highlights.

Off by default. The world is already tone mapped before this runs, so enabling this darkens the image overall unless you also lower Exposure.
sodium.options.tonemap_mode.name: Tonemap Curve
sodium.options.tonemap_mode.tooltip: Which curve to use when Tonemapping is enabled.
sodium.options.exposure.name: Exposure
sodium.options.exposure.tooltip:
Brightens the image before the tone curve is applied.

100% leaves the brightness unchanged.
